page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.gn5-c8g1.2xlarge is a GPU-accelerated server instance powered by an Intel Xeon E5-2682 v4 processor. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, operating at a base frequency of 2.5 GHz. The system is equipped with 60.0 GB of system memory, providing 7.5 GB per core. Acceleration is delivered via a single integrated NVIDIA Pascal P100 GPU with 16 GB of dedicated VRAM. Local storage consists of a 472 GB SSD, and the instance operates on a KVM hypervisor with a baseline network bandwidth of 3 Gbps.

Benchmark results show a clear divergence between CPU-bound tasks and GPU-accelerated workloads. The legacy Intel Broadwell CPU delivers modest performance, with stress-ng single-core and multi-core metrics falling into the bottom 10% and 25% respectively. Similarly, memory read bandwidth and Passmark database operations are relatively weak. However, the presence of the NVIDIA P100 GPU enables exceptional performance in specialized workloads. Large language model (LLM) inference benchmarks show top-tier results, achieving 316.69 tokens per second for prompt processing and 42.77 tokens per second for text generation on a medium 7B model.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, this instance represents a legacy GPU tier. While its raw CPU compute and memory bandwidth are uncompetitive compared to modern general-purpose instances, the bundled Pascal GPU and local SSD storage provide a cost-effective entry point for GPU-accelerated tasks without the premium pricing of newer architecture generations. The ecs.gn5-c8g1.2xlarge is best suited for workloads that can offload computation to the GPU, such as small-to-medium LLM inference, deep learning model training, and GPU-accelerated data processing, whereas it is poorly suited for CPU-heavy database operations or high-throughput memory-bound applications.
